newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zaire refugees, children trickle into Zambia.
newsitem.headline: Zaire refugees, children trickle into Zambia.

text.p: Refugees from Zaire, including unaccompanied children, are crossing the border into Zambia in a steady trickle but it could swell to a flood if there is a fight for the city of Lubumubashi, U.N. officials said on Wednesday.

An officer of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in the Zambian capital, Lusaka, said the agency would brace for up to 10,000 refugees if government troops and rebels clashed over Zaire's second largest city.
"We anticipate that, in the worst possible scenario, around 10,000 Zaireans could cross the border from around Lubumbashi," UNHCR protection officer Ron Mponda said.
"On the other hand, the influx of refugees could remain at the same level as now," he added.
Mponda said there had not been a significant increase in the number of Zaireans crossing the border from Lubumbashi since rebels started moving closer to the city.
"They are still coming in in trickles," Mponda said.
Recent arrivals from Zaire included 17 unaccompanied children, and a number of fleeing government soldiers.
"The number of soldiers that has come in is less than 100, and most have handed over their arms to the local authorities," Mponda said.
Zambia has granted some 3,000 Zaireans asylum since the rebels started their campaign in eastern Zaire in October 1996.
Several hundred Zaireans who crossed the border were granted passage to safer areas in Zaire.
